reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of TabRepo lies in replacing costly online AutoML with a dense offline repository of model evaluations. This allows GSE to perform zero-shot portfolio learning by selecting complementary configurations from a precomputed set. The normalized error formula provides a consistent metric for comparing diverse models across datasets, while the dense evaluation protocol ensures unbiased offline analysis. Greedy selection approximates an optimal subset of configurations that generalize well across unseen tasks. In GSI, this translates into constructing Bayesian prediction intervals for game outcomes using the normalized error as a calibration signal. For GSE, it enables dynamic ensemble instantiation based on historical performance without re-running expensive HPO. The key dualities involve: (1) online vs offline optimization, (2) sparse vs dense model evaluation, and (3) static vs adaptive model selection. Failure modes include non-stationarity of data distributions and overfitting to the fixed portfolio structure.
